previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and diastolic heart failure, was admitted for abdominal pain and shortness of breath. Imaging revealed colitis likely due to ischemia and new pleural effusions from acute on chronic heart failure, exacerbated by recent discontinuation of torsemide and dietary salt intake. He was treated with IV diuresis, restarted on torsemide, and managed for recurrent C. difficile infection with oral vancomycin. A urine culture grew vancomycin-resistant enterococcus, and he developed mild healthcare-associated pneumonia, both treated with Augmentin. A colonoscopy showed aphthous ulcers consistent with ischemic colitis and radiation proctitis, with incidental polyps to be addressed later. His condition improved, and he was discharged home with a planned antibiotic taper, follow-up colonoscopy, and instructions to monitor weight and symptoms.

history of atrial fibrillation and subtherapeutic INRs. TTE on 
___ could not rule out a cardiac thrombus at the posterior 
mitral annular calcification. Initially treated with heparin 
gtt. Once it was determined that patient did not need vascular 
surgery, patient restarted on aspirin and plavix. Because of his 
subtherapeutic INRs, he was switched to apixaban with discussion 
with his outpatient cardiologist. Initially, an LP was 
considered to rule out infectious etiologies causing his 
weakness such as PML. However, given that his weakness can be 
attributed to his strokes (emoblic nature explains fluctuating 
exam) and his weakness improved over time with normal neurologic 
exam at the time of discharge, LP was not felt to be indicated. 
He was followed by neurology during his hospital course. 
Evaluated by physical therapy who recommended rehab. Expected 
length of stay less than 30 days at rehab.

Patient has history of completely occluded right internal 
carotid artery. Evaluated by vascular surgery for endarterectomy 
given intracranial infarcts in the setting of severe carotid 
disease. However, based on carotid ultrasound and MRA of the 
brain and neck, decision was made not to proceed with surgery as 
his right carotid remained completely occluded whereas his left 
carotid was not stenosed to the degree that required 
intervention, and was not felt to be the source of his embolic 
CVA.
